# Google Play (9 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /app-search | `query` | 5 | Search Google Play apps by keyword |
| /search-suggestions | `query` | 1 | Get Google Play search suggestions |
| /app-info | `app_id` | 5 | Get full Google Play app details |
| /app-reviews | `app_id` | **5-9** | Get Google Play reviews for an app |
| /app-list | `app_collection` | 5 | Get a Google Play store chart |
| /app-listings-search | `title` | 10 | Search the Google Play listings database (paginated) |
| /categories | *(none)* | 1 | List Google Play app categories |
| /locations | `location_type`? | 1 | List supported Google Play storefront locations |
| /languages | *(none)* | 1 | List supported Google Play languages |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /app-search — 5cr

Returns a unified AppList of Google Play apps matching a keyword: title, icon, developer, rating, price/is_free, and store URL on every item, on the same canonical `App` shape used across every app marketplace (`app.store` = "google_play"). Detail-only fields (description, screenshots, installs) are null on search items; fetch /v1/google_play/app-info for the full record. Served from the Google Play catalogue: a first, uncached call is task-polled upstream and typically takes 3 to 15s, with a review pull at high `depth` reaching 40s. Set a client timeout of at least 60s.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword (e.g. 'photo editor').
- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name ('United States'), or a numeric location code ('2840'). Defaults to the US.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of results to retrieve (default 30, rounded up to multiples of 30, max 300). Note: Google Play's organic keyword search typically exposes only ~30 ranked results, so higher depth values rarely return more. To page deeper for app discovery, use /v1/google_play/app-listings-search (a filterable title/description database with real limit/offset/total).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search-suggestions — 1cr

Returns Google Play's search autocomplete suggestions for a keyword stem: the same terms the store's search box surfaces. The day Play starts autocompleting a phrase, real demand exists; poll a stem daily and diff to catch rising app keywords early. Each item is `{ term, priority }` ranked by Play's own order (Play exposes no numeric score). Returns a list under `items`.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Partial search keyword to autocomplete (e.g. 'reverse').
- `country` *(optional)*: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 storefront country code (e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'kr'). Defaults to 'us'. Anything that is not alpha-2 is rejected with a free 400; an unrecognised alpha-2 code is forwarded, and Google Play answers it with its default storefront rather than an error, so check the code if results look wrong for the market.
- `language` *(optional)*: ISO 639-1 language code. Defaults to 'en'.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/search-suggestions?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /app-info — 5cr

Returns the full canonical `App` record for one Google Play app keyed by its package name (`app_id`): title, description, developer block (incl. email/address/website), rating, price, install count + display ('1,000,000,000+'), version, size, screenshots, genres, chart tags, similar apps, and update date. The `app.store` field is always "google_play"; Apple-only leaves (advisories, languages) are null. Get the `app_id` from /v1/google_play/app-search.

**Parameters**

- `app_id`: Google Play package name (e.g. 'com.spotify.music'), from app-search.
- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-info?app_id=<app_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /app-reviews — 5-9cr

Returns a unified ReviewList of Google Play user reviews for an app, keyed by its package name (`app_id` on every review's `entity_id`). Each review carries the star rating, full text, reviewer name + avatar, helpful-vote count, developer `responses[]` (reply text + date), and publish date: on the SAME canonical `Review` shape used by Amazon, Google Shopping, and Trustpilot. Google reviews have no title (always null). `depth` returns reviews in batches of 150 (max 600).

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5-9 credits a call — budget the 9 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5-9 (metered): 5 credits per page. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.

**Parameters**

- `app_id`: Google Play package name (e.g. 'com.spotify.music'), from app-search.
- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of reviews to retrieve (default 150, batches of 150, max 600).
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Review ordering: `newest` (default) or `most_relevant`.
- `rating` *(optional)*: Filter to a single star rating (1-5). Verified working on this store (measured 06/09/2026: `rating=5` returns 150 five-star reviews, `rating=1` returns 150 one-star). The Apple App Store has no equivalent filter upstream.
- `label` *(optional)*: Optional CSV of SocialCrawl labels to add to every review. Without this param every page already carries sentiment and issue, free; label= adds the labels you name to them (the defaults keep running). sentiment and issue are free when asked for too; reports, incentivized and injection add 1 credit per started 25 newly judged reviews. judgments=off (or label=none) turns the default labels off. They read the review's title and text, never its stars. sentiment: how the reviewer feels, on five levels (level 0 to 4, score_0_1, confidence), plus rating_mismatch, true when the words clearly contradict the star rating (a glowing text under 1 star, a furious one under 5), null when the review has no rating. issue: the main problem the review reports (label: product_defect, sizing_or_fit, shipping_or_delivery, customer_service, price_or_value, missing_feature, other, or none, with confidence; label is null when unsure). reports (needs reports=): does this review say that the thing you describe happened (p, 0 to 1). incentivized: does the reviewer say they got the product free, discounted or rewarded for the review (p), and did the text carry a disclosure such as 'in exchange for my honest review', Vine or 체험단 (disclosed). injection flags text that addresses an AI system and tries to direct it (flagged, p); it never drops or rewrites a row. These are signals to read, never a verdict on a review or a reviewer. A review that could not be judged carries labels: null. Reviews already labelled for anyone are free, and so is a cached page. data.labels reports what was judged and billed.
- `reports` *(optional)*: Required by label=reports, ignored otherwise. What to look for, in plain words, up to 300 characters, for example reports=the battery drains quickly or reports=배송이 늦음. Every review gains labels.reports.p, the probability that it says so, in any wording or language. Without it label=reports is skipped with the warning label_reports_needs_reports and is not billed.
- `judgments` *(optional)*: Optional, on (the default) or off. By default every row gains free SocialCrawl judgments (computed.labels, and computed.relevance on search endpoints), reported in data.labels (mode default) and data.relevance (origin default), each with a status (complete, partial or skipped) and pending: the rows still being judged when the page was sent, which carry null now and are filled on your next call or cached read. Default judgments never add credits, never change an existing field, and never drop or reorder a row. off returns the page exactly as before, with none of those keys. label=none does the same.
- `dry_run` *(optional)*: Optional. When 1, return a cost preview for this labelled or relevance-filtered request without fetching the page or judging any row. data.estimate reports rows_expected, rows_cached, label_credits_min, label_credits_max and base_credits. 0 credits charged.
- `label_evidence` *(optional)*: Optional, only with label=. When 1, every labelled row also carries computed.labels_evidence.<preset> = { quote, sentence_index }: the sentence in the row that most clearly shows the label, copied verbatim. Absent or null when no single sentence shows it.
- `fit` *(optional)*: Optional. When goal, keep the rows and fields needed for the goal you pass in goal= (plus any that are uncertain, and the first and last), and replace the rest with a stub. data.held_back lists the held ids and a recall id that re-reads the full page from cache at no extra charge. Without this param the page is unchanged.
- `goal` *(optional)*: Required by fit=goal. What you are trying to do, in your own words, up to 300 characters.
- `fit_tokens` *(optional)*: Optional, only with fit=goal. Soft cap on how much of the page to keep, in tokens. Uncertain blocks and the first and last block are kept even if they exceed it.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-reviews?app_id=<app_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /app-list — 5cr

Returns a unified AppList for a Google Play store chart (top free, top paid, top grossing, movers & shakers, etc.), optionally scoped to a category. Each item is the same canonical `App` shape as app-search. Use it to track ranking movements or build a category leaderboard.

**Parameters**

- `app_collection`: Chart to retrieve: topselling_free, topselling_paid, topgrossing, movers_shakers, topselling_new_free, topselling_new_paid. An unknown value is rejected with a free 400 that lists the accepted set.
- `app_category` *(optional)*: Optional Google Play category to scope the chart (e.g. 'photography', 'game_puzzle').
- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of apps to retrieve (default 100, rounded up to multiples of 100, max 500). The store decides how deep a chart actually goes: measured 06/09/2026, `topselling_free` returns 100 at the default and 200 at depth=500, and `topselling_new_paid` has only 5 apps in it.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-list?app_collection=<app_collection>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /app-listings-search — 10cr

Searches a real-time, filterable Google Play listings database by app title (and/or description) and returns a unified AppList. Unlike the store-chart endpoints this one is the ONE true paginator: page by passing `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` until `pagination.has_more` is false, size the page with `limit` (≤50), and read the platform-wide match count at `data.total` (14,686 for the query 'photo editor' on 06/09/2026). Each row also carries `app.ext.appdata.time_update`, the freshness stamp for that listing in the database. Premium-tier because this surface is billed per returned item.

**Parameters**

- `title`: App title to search for (e.g. 'photo editor').
- `description` *(optional)*: Optional app-description text to match.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Apps per page (1-50, default 20).
- `offset` *(optional)*: Pagination offset (up to 10,000). Prefer `cursor`: pass `pagination.next_cursor` straight back and the offset is handled for you.
- `offset_token` *(optional)*: Legacy deep-pagination token. Prefer `cursor`, which accepts `pagination.next_cursor` verbatim and works on every paginatable endpoint. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead: the API maps it to this name for you.
- `filters` *(optional)*: Advanced filter expression as a JSON array of clauses, e.g. [["item.rating.value",">",4]]. Must be valid JSON and must be an array: anything else is rejected with a free 400 rather than silently returning an unfiltered page.
- `country` *(optional)*: Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim: the API maps it to this endpoint's native `offset_token` (cursor style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-listings-search?title=<title>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /categories — 1cr

Returns the list of Google Play app categories used by the `app_category` filter on /v1/google_play/app-list. Static reference data: heavily cached.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/categories" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /locations — 1cr

Returns the Google Play storefronts (name + numeric location code + ISO country code) accepted by the `country` param on every google_play endpoint: 211 countries. Static reference data, heavily cached. Storefronts are country-level, so a sub-country code resolves to its parent and returns that country's data: `country=1019999` (a Minnesota city) and `country=US` returned byte-identical charts on 06/09/2026. `location_type=all` returns the full underlying geo tree instead, all 269,681 rows of it (cities, postal codes, neighbourhoods, airports), which is a 46 MB response and rarely what you want here.

**Parameters**

- `location_type` *(optional)*: `country` (default) returns the storefronts the `country` param accepts. `all` returns the full underlying geo tree, including cities, postal codes and neighbourhoods, which all resolve to their parent country.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/locations" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /languages — 1cr

Returns the languages (name + code) supported by the Google Play App Data endpoints. Use a code as the `language` param. Static reference data: heavily cached.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/languages" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Google Play endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| What apps exist for this keyword? | `/app-search` | 5 |
| Cheap keyword expansion (what people type) | `/search-suggestions` | 1 |
| One app's full listing | `/app-info` | 5 |
| What users complain about | `/app-reviews` | 5 |
| Who is ranking in a category chart | `/app-list` | 5 |
| Deep, paginated listings-database search | `/app-listings-search` | **10** |
| Category / storefront / language reference | `/categories` · `/locations` · `/languages` | 1 |

### Use the 1cr endpoints to aim the 5cr ones

`/search-suggestions` (1cr) is store-autocomplete — real user queries, and the cheapest
keyword research in this platform. Confirm categories and storefronts with `/categories` and
`/locations` (1cr) before paying 5cr for a chart that may not exist in that market.

`/app-listings-search` (10cr) is for attribute-filtered database search; ordinary keyword
lookup is `/app-search` at 5cr.

### Pair with the App Store, or let Prism do it

This platform mirrors `app_store` endpoint-for-endpoint. To cover both stores you pay twice
and then have to title-match the same app across them yourself. `prism/apps-lookup` (30cr)
does the resolve-and-compare in one call; `prism/app-reviews` (15cr) returns cross-store
review intelligence, translated and clustered. For one or two apps the manual route is
cheaper; past that, Prism wins.
